summary:
Project ANTARIKSH CREW
// ASTRA Academy//

ASTRA Academy is an interactive space mission training and design simulator developed by Team ANTARIKSH CREW. Our project transforms space exploration into a hands on learning experience where users can explore the journey of an astronaut and understand how space missions are planned and operated.

The platform features four training phases: Mission Preparation, Launch Checks, Zero-Gravity Simulation, and Mission Debriefing. Users can also access the Mission Design Lab to create spacecraft concepts by selecting mission objectives, orbits, launch vehicles, scientific instruments, and essential spacecraft systems while balancing mass, power, communication and budget constraints.

To connect learning with real space science, we integrated NASA open data feeds for Near Earth Objects and space-weather notifications. An educational Mission Copilot provides guidance on mission planning and engineering decisions.

Our goal is to make space science more interactive, accessible, and engaging, inspiring students to understand the challenges of space exploration through simulation and experimentation.
details:
ASTRA Academy

ASTRA Academy is an interactive educational space-exploration and astronaut-training simulation developed to make space science, spacecraft engineering, and mission planning more interesting and accessible to students. The main purpose of this project is to provide users with a virtual experience of planning and preparing for a space mission while learning important scientific and engineering concepts.

The game guides users through different stages of a space mission, including destination selection, spacecraft preparation, pre-flight verification, a zero-gravity challenge, and mission design. Users can choose between three destinations: the Moon, Mars, and Europa. Each destination offers different mission durations, environmental conditions, and resource requirements.

During spacecraft preparation, players must manage a limited budget of 100 mission credits and a cargo allowance of 50 kg. They select essential equipment such as extended life support, precision thrusters, radiation shielding, scientific scanners, landing kits, and repair tools. This helps users understand the importance of resource management and decision-making in real space missions.

The project also includes a pre-flight checklist where users verify suit pressure, life-support systems, navigation, and propulsion. In the Zero-G Lab, players experience a simulated microgravity environment, navigate a spacecraft, collect scientific beacons, and learn how controlled thrust helps conserve fuel and maintain direction.

An additional Mission Design Studio allows users to explore spacecraft design and engineering concepts. It introduces five important mission constraints: mass, power, cost, data, and scientific value. The project also includes a Mission Copilot chatbot for educational guidance, NASA-related live data features, and mission-planning information inspired by NASA's published resources.

The game was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, making it accessible through a web browser. It uses interactive web elements, simulations, animations, and NASA open-data integrations, including NASA/JPL Near-Earth Object information and DONKI space-weather notifications. No specialised hardware is required; users can access the simulation using a computer or compatible mobile device with a web browser.

The creativity of ASTRA Academy lies in combining game-based learning with realistic space-mission planning concepts. Instead of simply reading about space exploration, students actively make decisions, manage limited resources, complete challenges, and understand the consequences of their choices.

The intended impact is to develop students' curiosity about space, scientific awareness, critical thinking, problem-solving, teamwork, and understanding of aerospace engineering. ASTRA Academy aims to make complex space-science concepts easier to understand through an engaging and interactive learning experience.
